## What AffineDrift Is {#what-it-is}

AffineDrift is a free, open notebook about how a golf swing moves and why. It uses physics models to split each moment of the swing into what the body and club would do on their own and what the golfer adds. Each page says how strong its evidence is, so you can judge each claim for yourself.

## The Big Idea in One Picture {#big-idea}

Picture a swing as a point moving across a map of every possible state. At each point, two arrows add up. One arrow is the drift: where gravity and momentum would carry the motion with no effort at all. The other is the push: the change the golfer's muscles add. The picture below draws both arrows from a simple pendulum model.

{{< include ../_includes/generated/drift-plus-control.qmd >}}

The point of the split is not that one arrow matters more. It is that you can only ask "what did the golfer add?" once you know what would have happened anyway. [The Big Idea in Five Minutes](../pages/big-idea.html) explains it with everyday examples, and the [Overview](../pages/overview.html) explains the scope of the site in more detail.

## How to Read the Evidence Labels {#evidence-labels}

Pages and claims carry a label that says how far they have been checked. Read the label before you trust a claim.

- **Available**: the text or code is done and open to read. Nobody outside has checked it yet.
- **Validated**: the claim names real test data and its error bounds. Nearby claims do not share the label.
- **Experimental**: early work, shared so people can test and discuss it.
- **Planned**: the work is described but not done.
- **Deprecated**: kept for the record. Do not use it for new work.
- **Opinion**: the author's view, not a proof or a measurement.

A separate [evidence ladder](../pages/how-to-read.html#evidence-ladder) says how strong the support is, from pure math up to tests on real people. The full definitions are in [How to Read This Site](../pages/how-to-read.html#publication-states).

## What This Site Is Not {#what-it-is-not}

- **It is not coaching advice.** The models explain motion. They do not tell you how to swing.
- **It is not peer reviewed by default.** A page being online means you can read and check it. It does not mean experts have signed off on it.
- **It is not a validated model of a human.** Most results come from simple models of links and joints. They are tools for thinking, not a measured picture of any real golfer.
